verdict.rationale: Kino's desktop app runs its own MCP server, so external agents can search footage and edit projects. Agents can also make cuts and answer review comments, so a meaningful slice of the UI is programmatically reachable. Nothing documents a general API or claims full UI parity, and the WYSIWYG editor is presented as where you 'tweak any detail', which suggests some control stays UI-first. Missing for 10: a documented public API or MCP tool reference, an explicit UI-parity statement, documented programmatic coverage of sharing, review links, smart bins, templates and fine-grained edits, and independent hands-on confirmation of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The desktop app runs an MCP server, so ChatGPT, Claude Code, Codex and Cursor can search your footage and edit your projects from their own chat.
Comments land on your timeline, and the agent can answer them.
The agent reads your footage, makes the edit, and leaves every clip on the timeline for you to move.
